answer.rationale: Rollback is precluded by compliance since the release contains a mandatory security patch. The presenting symptom (write-path p99 climbing 5x under heavy settlement traffic at daily peak) matches the pattern in memory_b3, where provisioning headroom before a retail peak absorbed surge and kept queue depth flat, rather than the failover, circuit-breaker, or read-replica scenarios which addressed different failure modes (regional outage, dependency failure, read/dashboard contention respectively). Read replicas and circuit breakers don't relieve write-path pressure, and failover risks losing in-flight settlement writes during a peak-traffic window, conflicting with the objective of not losing customer writes. Verifying memory_b3's archived source confirms it genuinely addressed a write-capacity/queue scenario before committing capacity as the one available intervention. I'm treating this as a standard, monitored capacity increase rather than a full broad rollout, since we can't also run a second intervention this window and need to watch for any unexpected interaction with the new release under peak settlement load.
